title: Cone straightening sends right anodyne maps to equivalences and recovers fibers
statement:
Use simplicial sets and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and simplicial categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], in fixed universes enlarged when needed. Define $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ to have objects $0,\ldots,m$, mapping simplicial set from $i$ to $j$ the nerve of the inclusion poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing both endpoints if $i\leq j$, and the empty simplicial set otherwise. Composition is union. Monotone maps act by images of subsets, and $\mathfrak C[S]=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^m\to S}\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ in simplicial categories. For a simplicial set $X$, define the join cone $X\star\Delta^0$ by $(X\star\Delta^0)_r=X_r\amalg\{v_r\}\amalg\coprod_{0\leq u<r}X_u$, where $v_r$ is the constant cone simplex. A mixed simplex indexed by $u$ has its first $u+1$ vertices in $X$ and its remaining vertices at $v$; operators restrict this ordered concatenation, using the operators of $X$ on the initial part and giving a pure simplex when one part becomes empty. For any simplicial map $a:X\to S$, put $M_a=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[S]$, and let $v$ denote its new cone vertex. Define $\operatorname{St}_S(X)(s)=M_a(s,v)$, a simplicial functor $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ by precomposition. This construction is functorial in $X$ over $S$ and preserves small colimits in $X$. For a vertex $t$ of $S$, there is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{St}_S(\{t\})(s)\cong\mathfrak C[S](s,t)$: compose with the adjoined arrow $t\to v$.

Use right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. For any right anodyne map $j:X\to Y$ over any simplicial set $S$, the map $\operatorname{St}_S(j)(s)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $s$ of $S$.

A right fibration $a:X\to S$ means a map with the right lifting property against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$. For every such $a$ and vertex $s$ of $S$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(X_s)(*)\longrightarrow\operatorname{St}_S(X)(s),\qquad X_s=X\times_S\{s\},$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. It is induced by the inclusion of the fiber, the cone construction and the map $\{s\}\to S$; it is natural in maps of right fibrations and their base vertices. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ and no Kan hypothesis on $X$ are imposed.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, definition and Proposition 2.2.1.1; Theorem 2.2.1.2 (Quillen assertion), Proposition 2.1.4.9 and Remark 2.1.4.12 (right anodyne maps are contravariant trivial cofibrations); Proposition 2.2.3.15 (fiber comparison), printed pp. 73-74 and 87. No Stacks tag states unmarked straightening.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] with $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\phi$ the identity. Its $M_{a,\phi}$ is exactly the pushout $M_a$ in the item, so its left adjoint is the specified $\operatorname{St}_S$. This proves functoriality and preservation of all small colimits, including the empty one, by the adjunction: maps from $\operatorname{St}_S(\operatorname{colim}X_i)$ to $F$ correspond to maps from the colimit to $U_SF$, hence compatible families of maps from $\operatorname{St}_S(X_i)$ to $F$. For a single vertex $t$, the attached category is the interval $t\to v$. In the pushout no arrow leaves $v$ except its identity. Thus every arrow from $s$ to $v$ is uniquely a mapping simplex in $\mathfrak C[S](s,t)$ followed by $t\to v$; composition relations identify consecutive old arrows by their old composition. This gives the displayed isomorphism, in each simplicial degree and compatibly with operators.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, definition and the adjunction; representable case by the pushout universal property.

proof.text: In the contravariant model structure supplied by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model], the given right anodyne $j$ is a trivial cofibration over $S$. The left Quillen assertion of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], at the identity $\phi$, makes $\operatorname{St}_S(j)$ a projective trivial cofibration. The weak equivalences of that projective model structure are defined objectwise, so each $\operatorname{St}_S(j)(s)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This argument uses no assumption on $S$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.9(1), dualized; Theorem 2.2.1.2, Quillen adjunction assertion.

proof.text: Write $V(K)=\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(K)(*)$. By Step 1 it preserves colimits. To identify its value on a simplex, first check that $\mathfrak C$ preserves pushouts directly from its defining colimit in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. For any small simplicial category $A$, set $R(A)_m=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(\mathfrak C[\Delta^m],A)$, with operators given by precomposition. A functor $\mathfrak C[K]\to A$ is exactly a compatible family of functors from the $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ indexed by simplices of $K$, hence exactly a simplicial map $K\to R(A)$. This natural bijection makes $\mathfrak C$ a left adjoint, so it preserves the pushout defining $J^n$. Consequently $V(\Delta^n)=\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)=Q^n$: the whole initial face is sent to the unique base object. These identifications commute with every simplex operator. Hence $V(K)=|K|_Q$, the quotient of $\coprod_nK_n\times Q^n$ by the simplex-operator relations. Maps out of this quotient are compatible maps from its copies of $Q^n$, giving the adjunction $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$. The same node supplies the natural map $Q^n\to\Delta^n$, degreewise injective latching maps, $Q^0=\Delta^0$, and weak contractibility of all $Q^n$. As $\partial\Delta^n$ is the colimit of its proper faces, $V(\partial\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^n)$ is precisely that latching monomorphism. Every $V(\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^0)$ is a weak equivalence since both terms are nonempty weakly contractible. The Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the boundary-collapse test [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] now show that $V$ is left Quillen and preserves all weak homotopy equivalences.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, construction of Q; Proposition 2.2.2.9, Quillen adjunction part, with the existing boundary-collapse criterion.

proof.text: The natural maps $Q^n\to\Delta^n$ induce $p_K:V(K)\to K$. We prove they are weak equivalences by skeleta. The empty case is the identity. In dimension zero, $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$ and $Q^0=\Delta^0$, so the comparison on every zero-skeleton is the identity on its coproduct of points. At a skeletal successor, [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] expresses the attachment as a pushout of a coproduct of $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Step 3 takes it to a pushout with a monomorphic attaching map. Induct on dimension: $p_{\partial\Delta^n}$ is covered by the earlier dimensions; $p_{\Delta^n}$ is a weak equivalence because its two sides are nonempty weakly contractible: for $Q^n$ this is [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], while the realization of $\Delta^n$ contracts to its last vertex by the straight-line homotopy in the standard topological simplex. Coproducts of these maps are weak equivalences since realizations are disjoint unions, with components and based homotopy groups computed within one summand. The pushout assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] proves the successor comparison. Its filtered-colimit assertion proves the comparison at the colimit of skeleta, since $V$ preserves colimits and naturality identifies the colimit of the skeletal comparisons with $p_K$. This proves $p_K$ for arbitrary small $K$, without requiring finiteness or a Kan condition.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, skeletal induction, with arbitrary coproducts and the filtered skeletal colimit made explicit.

proof.text: In the Kan model structure every object is cofibrant, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. By Step 4, the left derived functor of $V$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity, so it is an equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] to $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ of Step 3. If $T$ is Kan, the actual evaluation counit $\epsilon_T:V\operatorname{Sing}_Q(T)\to T$ is a weak equivalence: the target is fibrant and the right-adjoint value is cofibrant. Explicitly on a generator indexed by $u:Q^n\to T$ it is $q\mapsto u(q)$. These are the actual maps used below, not an unspecified isomorphism in the homotopy category.

Let $X\to S$ be the given right fibration. Choose a projective fibrant replacement $r:\operatorname{St}_SX\to F$, using the model structure and functorial factorization in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. In particular $r(s)$ is a weak equivalence and $F(s)$ is Kan. Every $X\to S$ is cofibrant by the monomorphism description of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. At identity $\phi$ the Quillen equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] therefore says the adjoint $h:X\to U_SF$ of $r$ is a contravariant weak equivalence. Both objects are right fibrations, the first by hypothesis and the second by the right-adjoint assertion. Fiberwise detection in [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] gives a weak equivalence $h_s:X_s\to(U_SF)_s\cong\operatorname{Sing}_QF(s)$. Step 3 gives that $V(h_s)$ is a weak equivalence; Step 5 gives that $\epsilon_{F(s)}$ is a weak equivalence. By the fiber/adjunction compatibility stated in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], their composite is exactly $r(s)\phi_s$, where $\phi_s:V(X_s)\to\operatorname{St}_SX(s)$ is the comparison in the item. Concretely a generator $(z,q)$ with $z\in(X_s)_n$ and $q\in Q^n$ is sent first to $(h_s(z),q)$ and then to $h_s(z)(q)$; the definition of the adjoint identifies this with applying $r(s)$ to the cone arrow determined by $(z,q)$. Thus the equality holds on generators and descends through all operator relations. Two-out-of-three now makes this specified $\phi_s$ a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.15, proof; Corollary 2.2.3.13 for fiberwise detection and Remark 2.2.2.11 for the exact fiber identity.

proof.text: The comparison itself needs no fibrant replacement choices: it is the map on cone pushouts induced by $X_s\to X$ and $\{s\}\to S$. For a commutative square of right fibrations $X\to Y$ over $f:S\to T$, with $f(s)=t$, there is a strict map $X_s\to Y_t$. On a generator $(z,q)$ of $V(X_s)$ both composites around the naturality square take the mapping simplex $q$ through the same functor $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to M_Y$ associated to the image of $z$. The equality is compatible with faces and degeneracies, and with composition by old arrows; it therefore descends to the pushouts and coends. This proves naturality for pointed base maps and in particular for maps over a fixed base. The model and Quillen inputs were stated for arbitrary simplicial bases; neither Step 6 nor this construction assumes that $S$ is a quasicategory or that $X$ is Kan. Empty fibers cause no exception in the argument, since $V(\varnothing)=\varnothing$ and all the model-category criteria allow empty simplicial sets.
